messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for feature `prompt-routing-v2` to canary pool started at 03:02 UTC. 10% traffic. /cc @michelle (oncall)
pagerduty-bot: Paging michelle (oncall) — anomaly detected: request error rate spike on /v1/prompt-route (alert id: PD-8932)
michelle (oncall): saw the page, joining. quick check: is this the new prompt-routing path?
aj (eng-sre): yes, matches canary. I'm with Sam. Initial graphs show 500s jump ~03:06, latency up ~700ms for canary hosts only.
sam (runtime): logs from canary: lots of "kv-cache-mismatch" and model-init timeouts. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:06:12Z ERROR prompt-router handler failed: kv-cache-mismatch: expected key=abc123, found nil
2026-03-15T03:06:15Z WARN model-loader timeout (3000ms) for model id: open-rwd-7b-quant
```
michelle (oncall): what's customer impact? public API customers? any high-traffic ones?
natalie (product): quick triage from support: a small PLG cohort (10 orgs) saw elevated errors, a few internal trial accounts too. Not global but 15% error rate on canary traffic.
aj (eng-sre): severity P1 for canary -> risk of rollout causing wider outage if not contained. Recommend kill-switch to route canary traffic back to `prompt-routing-v1` and pause rollout.
sam (runtime): agreed. I can flip feature flag. Using LaunchDarkly CLI: `ld-ctl toggle --env prod --flag prompt-routing-v2 --off --staged canary`
michelle (oncall): do it. also put a quick runbook step: confirm traffic shifts and monitor 5m.
ld-bot: Request received: toggle prompt-routing-v2 -> OFF (requested by michelle). Executing...
ld-bot: Toggle completed. Flag `prompt-routing-v2` is now OFF for canary group.
sam (runtime): confirming on proxies: `curl -sS http://lb.internal/health?route=prompt-route | jq .route` -> `prompt-routing-v1` for canary host 10.12.5.67
aj (eng-sre): metrics: error rate returning to baseline on canary within two minutes. rolling back in-progress canary pods to previous config as well.
michelle (oncall): michelle -> aj handoff: I'm on a 10-min ride, aj pls own postmortem and coord with product.
aj (eng-sre): taking ownership. will keep this incident open for 60m for verification, then mark RESOLVED. Assigning follow-ups: investigate kv-cache invalidation in startup path, add better fallback when model-loader times out, add alert threshold for canary-specific latency.
natalie (product): notifying affected customers with a short note: "We observed elevated errors for prompt-routing during an experimental canary. Traffic has been routed back to the stable path and the rollout paused. We're investigating and will follow up."
michelle (oncall): quick note for postmortem: timeline, flag flip command, logs above, impacted orgs list (internal doc link: https://redwood.internal/notes/INC-1757890123) :thumbsup:
aj (eng-sre): will collect logs and create a postmortem doc. early hypothesis: kv-cache hash version mismatch between compiled kernels used by canary build and runtime cache format -> leads to null keys and model init slow-path.
sam (runtime): also noticed increased GC churn on canary hosts — maybe new quantization changes. will add profiling.
ld-bot: reminder: flag change recorded (audit id: LD-2026-0456).
michelle (oncall): FYI I tagged this incident in PagerDuty as "resolved by kill-switch" once metrics stabilized. leaving notes for follow-up. handing back to aj.
aj (eng-sre): thanks — continuing investigation; will post updates here. closing timeline note: feature rollout paused and canary traffic restored at 03:14 UTC.
michelle (oncall): thanks team.
aj (eng-sre): update 03:45 UTC: root cause narrowed to runtime/quant mismatch, creating ticket ENG-4921. Will schedule canary rework and stricter pre-rollout checks.
michelle (oncall): marking incident as monitoring. last check 03:50 UTC: no regression seen.
michelle (oncall): closing thread at 03:54 UTC if no new signals. :white_check_mark:
